method: per-kind probe (ls dist/types/<root>/, file counts, exported-symbol extraction), cross-checked against asupersync's concurrency surface and our crates' actual async/Cx usage on disk
positive_control: async (3 files): the ONLY root where OMP's surface and OUR binding dependency (asupersync) address the same concern (concurrency/cancellation). Fully mapped: every exported type examined, every interaction with asupersync assessed. If this root is not fully covered, the wave's first question is unanswered.
anti_vacuity: 6 roots enumerated with file counts and export symbols; zero-surface enumeration impossible

rows.omp_alternative: AsyncJobManager/AsyncJob/AsyncJobDeliverySink/AsyncJobFilter — OMP's background-job manager with delivery-state tracking and reaping. OUR asupersync contract covers the same ground: Cx cancellation (cx.cancel_with), checkpoint-in-loops, region-owned tasks (no detached spawns), and the timeout-is-not-a-verdict rule. The two models are COMPATIBLE but different: asupersync uses &Cx first + obligation ledger; omp uses an owned manager with filter/reap. We depend on omp's async runtime running correctly (every pane session uses it), tested by the RPC probe reaching agent_end on the wire (§11.9).
CpuProfile/CpuProfileCallFrame/ChangelogEntry/BlockContextSource — OMP's internal utilities (profiling, changelog, block context). No crate's job is to consume omp's internal utility types
rows.refusal: no consumer; these are product-internal helpers

rows.omp_alternative: XAICredentials (provider: xai-oauth|xai, apiKey, baseURL) — model provider credential config for xAI. Product-internal credential wiring; our credentials are managed separately
rows.refusal: no consumer; credential management is our own concern

rows.omp_alternative: TinyTitleLocalModelSpec, ONLINE_TINY_TITLE_MODEL_KEY, DEFAULT_TINY_TITLE_LOCAL_MODEL_KEY — omp's on-device session-title model (lfm2-700m, q4 dtype). Session titles are the agent's internal concern; no crate consumes them
VibeModeState (enabled: boolean) — omp's vibe mode session state, mirroring plan-mode state. No crate reads or sets vibe mode

classifyDifficulty — per-prompt difficulty classifier for the auto thinking level (maps prompts to low/medium/high/xhigh effort). The agent's internal model selection; the orchestrator does not classify prompt difficulty

first_question_answered: async COMPOSES with asupersync, does not conflict. OMP's AsyncJobManager runs INSIDE each omp session (managing that session's background jobs). Our asupersync Cx runs OUTSIDE in the orchestrator (managing the supervisor's subprocess lifecycle). They never touch: omp's internal async is invisible to us, and our subprocess management is invisible to omp. The seam is the rpc transport (omp-rpc-session), which uses OUR Cx for the SSH/child-process side and sends JSON-RPC over the wire. No duplication detected.
